answer: Staking protocols implement an onyx hardware anchor to tether digital identity, forcing a quill of cryptographic proofs to validate agent sincerity. By mandating collateral lockup equal to the network value, an attacker faces strictly negative expected utility. This capital barrier renders mass Sybil creation prohibitively expensive. Consequently, the system achieves a Nash equilibrium where Byzantine agents are incentivized to maintain honest consensus, ensuring protocol stability.
